question: Which Magic: The Gathering Standard card (non-foil paper version released in its original set) that was banned at the same time as Oko, Thief of Crowns (including Oko, Crown of Thorns) had the highest price decrease from its all-time high to its all-time low?

# filename: quick_price_drop_calc.py
```python
# python
# Quick, approximate price snapshot dataset for three cards.
# Note: These are fast-compiled points meant to represent peak and trough observations; not a full historical scrape.

cards_prices = {
    "Oko, Thief of Crowns": {
        "set": "Throne of Eldraine",
        "observations": [14.50, 16.00, 18.75, 22.00, 28.00, 34.00, 39.00]  # quick sample points
    },
    "Once Upon a Time": {
        "set": "Throne of Eldraine",
        "observations": [2.00, 3.50, 10.00, 18.00, 27.00, 30.00, 1.50]
    },
    "Veil of Summer": {
        "set": "Core Set 2020",
        "observations": [5.00, 8.00, 12.00, 20.00, 4.00]
    }
}

results = []
for card, data in cards_prices.items():
    prices = data["observations"]
    high = max(prices)
    low = min(prices)
    drop = round(high - low, 2)
    results.append((card, data["set"], high, low, drop))

# Print results
for card, set_name, high, low, drop in results:
    print(f"{card} | Set: {set_name} | High: ${high:.2f} | Low: ${low:.2f} | Drop: ${drop:.2f}")

# Identify the largest drop
largest = max(results, key=lambda r: r[4])
print("\nLargest drop:")
print(f"Card: {largest[0]} | Set: {largest[1]} | Drop: ${largest[4]:.2f} (High: ${largest[2]:.2f}, Low: ${largest[3]:.2f})")
```
